channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
item.description: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

item.title: [DW] British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
item.description: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

item.title: [DW] UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
item.description: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

item.title: [DW] Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
item.description: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

item.title: [DW] Iran denies role in fridge hack, France summons ambassador
item.description: France has said it rules "nothing" out in response to a cyberattack on supermarket refrigeration units. Iran, however, said it categorically rejected Paris' "baseless and one-sided accusations" of IRGC involvement.

item.title: [DW] Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM
item.description: At least 12 people were killed and dozens injured in a series of crashes caused by thick fog in Bulgaria. Police, firefighters and paramedics were dispatched to the scene for the rescue operation.

item.title: [DW] Fact check: Online disinformation rife after Krakow mass shooting
item.description: Fake and AI-manipulated images spread online in the hours after the Krakow attack, fueling false narratives about the mass shooting. DW Fact Check examined what's real, and what isn't.

item.title: [DW] US, Russia, Ukraine wrap up talks with prisoner exchange agreement
item.description: Peace talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US concluded in the United Arab Emirates. The two day talks were the first such meeting since February. DW has the latest updates.

item.title: [DW] EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
item.description: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s self-styled pacifists are helping Putin freeze Ukrainians in their homes
item.description: As Russia bombs Ukraine’s grid, Hungary, Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Bulgaria want to opt out of the next EU loan - money that actually also helps Ukrainian's civilians build back-up power and heating.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Parliament asked to lift immunity of German far-right MEP accused of baseball‑bat attack on teen
item.description: The EU parliament was requested to waive a German far-right MEP’s immunity to allow his prosecution for drunk-driving and violently assaulting minors with a baseball bat.

item.title: [EU Observer] With Russia’s front collapsing, Putin is weaponising the Dnipro River by using it to slice Ukraine in two (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,722)
item.description: Ukraine’s commanders warn that if bridges fall, cities are evacuated and Patriots stay empty, the war could shift from the front lines to a desperate race to stop a 1,000‑km river from becoming an internal border.

item.title: [DW] Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
item.description: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

item.title: [EU Observer] EU’s Kallas wants next week’s UK‑EU summit to kick‑start ‘small steps’ to rejoin
item.description: The UK has a shopping list of sectoral agreements it wants to come away with from next week's key and long-delayed EU-UK summit, part of the 'small steps' in a path that could eventually lead to membership.

item.title: [EU Observer] From pin-up calendars to the Istanbul Convention: Magyar’s U-turn, as Operation Purgatory reaches Orbán’s brother (Day 184 of the Tisza government)
item.description: Hungary’s political landscape is shifting dramatically as the new Tisza government challenges Viktor Orbán’s 16-year legacy. With Orbán’s brother facing detention, Fidesz support plunging to historic lows and corruption investigations gaining public backing, the country is entering a new political chapter. The government has also announced ambitious gender-equality measures, including stronger protections against domestic viol

item.title: [DW] What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
item.description: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

item.title: [DW] Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
item.description: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

item.title: [EU Observer] Fastest EU citizens’ initiative ever pushes Brussels to end EU‑Israel trade agreement
item.description: Over one million Europeans back the ending of the EU-Israel trade agreement, in the latest citizen effort to hold European governments to account for their human rights commitments. Now the EU Commission has up to six months to respond.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU commissioner vows to use ‘all relevant tools’ to protect media freedom as Babiš public broadcasting bill alarms MEPs
item.description: MEPs spoke out against the Czech government's controversial broadcasting overhaul, while commissioner Michael McGrath said he would use “all relevant tools” to protect media freedom. Czechs in Brussels gathered outside parliament to protest.

item.title: [DW] UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
item.description: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s youth take to the streets as the post‑war promise of a better life breaks down
item.description: Europe's teenagers and students still believe in politics - but are turning away from parliaments and towards the streets. Hardly surprising, when the traditional milestones of adulthood – a degree, a stable job, a home and financial independence – are seem increasingly out of reach.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU goes to Syria to talk business amid wider worries over lingering Russian influence and Jordanian attack
item.description: The EU is spearheading efforts next week to get Syria back on its feet, followed by an investment conference in Jordan. But Russian influence and recent lethal Jordanian fighter-jet attacks in southern Syria point to lingering issues.

item.description: A night that cost Russia three of its own aircraft, a Ukrainian pilot felling nine drones with a single F-16 sortie, and a supposed humanitarian corridor that could help Moscow tighten its grip on Kostiantynivka together paint a war where every tactical success hides a dangerous twist.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘Do not be afraid, be prepared’: Estonian prime minister Kristen Michal on how to defend Europe from Russia
item.description: Estonian prime minister Kristen Michal lays out how to build up Europe's defences. He also urges the use of Russian assets frozen in Belgium, and discussed Baltic expertise in fighting Vladimir Putin.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Is the right to protest under threat in Europe?
item.description: In France, the Senate has just adopted a draft bill that could severely restrict the right to protest. The text still has to go through the National Assembly, but it stands a good chance of becoming law.

item.title: [DW] Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
item.description: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
